scores.evidence: Build vs buy: no third-party CI product fits the 50-service, custom-rollback, secret-injection scope without heavy modification; build is forced.
scores.rationale: Several errors: Vault transit "encrypts secrets in transit" misstated, Vault static auth for prod, "dual-write" for CI transition is incoherent, reverse-image pull rollback ignores schema state, webhook IP whitelist/static secret.

scores.evidence: Ramp 40 services in waves of 5–10 (two per week, blitzing on Friday); each wave runs its pipeline on the new platform before the old pipeline is disabled.
scores.rationale: Covers main sequencing with pilot and waves, but claims build is forced with no justification, misses the service inventory, and the Phase 3 timeline with 40 services plus the 2-week cutover is loosely specified.

scores.evidence: Platform runs on a single host ... Monolithic controller + remote runners; Phase 0 'stateless' controller yet also 'Phase 3 cutover: all 50 for 2 weeks'
scores.rationale: Recognizable design, but contradictions: Vault choice 'static team credentials' vs service-scoped policies, Phase 0 'production' vs dev, wave-based onboarding vs 'cutover of all 50' gate, single-node SPOF vs 99.5% SLO.

scores.evidence: Inject a failure mid-rollback, verify the rollback succeeds and the old version is live
scores.rationale: Validation is tied to risks with early spike, pilot, and measurable gates, though thresholds are largely invented and lacks contract, supply chain, flaky tests checks.

scores.evidence: ASSUMPTION: developer velocity at 5–10 min feedback is standard
scores.rationale: Assumptions are labeled with revisit triggers and missing inputs, though some assertions (e.g. 'REQUIREMENT: stated by ops team', $500/month) are invented.

scores.evidence: Canary rollback is automatic if error rate > baseline + 5% for 2 min; manual override is also possible.
scores.rationale: Covers rollback, Vault seal, platform SPOF, secrets redaction, but misses untrusted PRs, supply chain, flaky tests, DB migration failure modes, duplicates.

scores.evidence: on-call playbooks for common alerts (queue depth, Vault seal, artifact store full)
scores.rationale: Observability, GitOps rollback, runbooks and IaC exist but ownership is thin, 2 FTE for 50 services with self-hosted Vault is optimistic, and single-node controller.
Only storage cost is budgeted; compute/runner cost, the dominant driver, is not estimated and the hosted vs self-hosted claim is unsupported.

scores.evidence: Monolith vs services ... Reversibility R3: all 50 services adopt; schema baked into configs
scores.rationale: Decision table explicitly rates reversibility and schema spike validates the hardest-to-undo choice early, though build-forced and Vault lock-in are little examined.

scores.evidence: Build vs buy: ... build is forced.
scores.rationale: Mostly proportionate phasing, but self-hosting Vault HA, canary via service mesh and a custom controller add unjustified complexity for the need.

scores.evidence: Two-week spike (parallel to Phase 0): define the config schema on paper, code the validator, and test it against the actual build configs of 6 sampled services
scores.rationale: Ordered phases with concrete tasks and exit checks and fallback; some vagueness around the controller implementation.

checklist.evidence: sampled across tech stacks: Node, Go, Python, Java ... Define the config schema (YAML) for a service pipeline
Ramp 40 services in waves of 5–10 ... each wave runs its pipeline on the new platform before the old pipeline is disabled.
Reverse-image pull (revert to the previous tagged image in the registry)
HashiCorp Vault + static team credentials (no service-to-service yet)
Implement traffic-split ... 5% of traffic, measure error rates and latency, expand to 25% then 100% or rollback.
Build a staging environment (mirror of dev; services run on dedicated cluster or namespace).
Pipeline latency (commit to feedback) | p95 < 5 min
Self-hosted runners on a single cluster (gated by single-node SPOF risk)
Set up SLIs and burn-rate alerts: measure platform availability and pipeline success rate
Capture audit logs: every secret read, every deployment, every rollback is logged with timestamp and operator

traps.evidence: Rollback: If V5 fails ... those services revert to the old pipeline; The old CI system is kept as a standby for 2 weeks
Reverse-image pull (revert to the previous tagged image in the registry)
HashiCorp Vault + static team credentials (no service-to-service yet)
if one service's build fails, others are unaffected; no cascading failure
no third-party CI product fits the 50-service, custom-rollback, secret-injection scope without heavy modification; build is forced.

note: A phased, pilot-first plan with good gates and reversibility tables, but it skips supply-chain security, immutable artifact promotion, contract testing, flaky tests and compute cost, and it leans toward building a custom controller.
